name: Power Automate
description: Connect your own Power Platform environment (Dataverse) to see and manage your Power Automate cloud flows from Imperal -- list flows with their status, create/update/delete them, turn them on or off, inspect and cancel/resubmit their runs, and run bulk operations across many flows at once. Uses your own Azure AD App Registration (Application User) -- nothing is hosted or proxied by Imperal beyond the request itself. Note: this connects to flows added to a Dataverse Solution; personal "My Flows" not added to a Solution are not reachable by Microsoft's own management API and are out of scope here.

tools.name: connect_power_automate
tools.description: Connect a Microsoft Power Platform environment by saving your Azure AD App Registration credentials (tenant_id, client_id, client_secret) and your Dataverse environment_url/environment_id, after checking they actually work together. You'll need: an Azure AD App Registration (Azure Portal > Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations), a client secret created under Certificates & secrets, and that app registered as an Application User in your Power Platform environment with a security role granting workflow privileges. Note: this only manages Solution-aware cloud flows -- personal unattached "My Flows" are not supported by Microsoft's own Web API and are out of scope here.

tenant_id.description: Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) tenant ID that owns your Power Platform environment.
tenant_id.title: Tenant Id

client_id.description: Application (client) ID of the Azure AD App Registration created for this connection.
client_id.title: Client Id

client_secret.description: Client secret value of the Azure AD App Registration. Create it under Certificates & secrets.
client_secret.title: Client Secret

environment_url.description: Your Dataverse environment URL, e.g. https://org12345.crm.dynamics.com. Found in the Power Platform admin center under the environment's details.
environment_url.title: Environment Url

environment_id.description: Your Power Platform environment ID (a GUID), used for the flow-runs REST API. Found in the Power Platform admin center under the environment's details.
environment_id.title: Environment Id

label.description: Optional friendly name for this environment connection.
label.title: Label

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the Power Platform environments currently connected.

params_schema.description: Explicit empty params model -- V17 disallows untyped handlers.
params_schema.title: NoParams

tools.name: disconnect_power_automate
tools.description: Disconnect one Power Platform environment: deletes its saved Azure AD credentials. Existing flows and their runs in that environment are not affected -- only Webbee's access to them is removed.

connection_id.description: Connection id to disconnect, from list_connections.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

tools.name: list_flows
tools.description: List cloud flows (Solution-aware) in a connected Power Platform environment, via the Dataverse Web API. Personal unattached "My Flows" are not returned -- Microsoft's Web API does not expose them.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

state.description: Filter by state: 'draft', 'activated', or 'suspended'. Omit for all.
state.title: State

tools.name: get_flow
tools.description: Read one cloud flow in full from the Dataverse Web API.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

tools.name: create_flow
tools.description: Create a new Solution-aware cloud flow in the Dataverse `workflow` table. clientdata must be valid Power Automate flow definition JSON (the format Power Automate itself exports/imports) -- this connector does not validate its internal shape, only that it is well-formed JSON. New flows are created in Draft state; call set_flow_state to activate.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

name.description: Display name for the new flow.
name.title: Name

clientdata.description: String-encoded JSON of the flow definition and its connectionReferences (the same shape the Power Automate designer produces). Must be a valid, complete flow definition.
clientdata.title: Clientdata

activate.description: Create the flow already turned on (Activated) instead of Draft.
activate.title: Activate

tools.name: update_flow
tools.description: Update selected fields of an existing cloud flow (name, description, and/or its clientdata definition) without touching omitted fields.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

clientdata.description: New string-encoded JSON flow definition, replacing the current one.
clientdata.title: Clientdata

tools.name: delete_flow
tools.description: Permanently delete a cloud flow from Dataverse. Cannot be undone.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

workflow_id.description: Dataverse workflowid (GUID) of the flow to permanently delete.
workflow_id.title: Workflow Id

tools.name: set_flow_state
tools.description: Turn a cloud flow on (activated) or off (suspended/draft) by setting its Dataverse statecode/statuscode.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

tools.name: list_flow_runs
tools.description: List recent runs of a cloud flow, via the Power Platform REST API (a separate, newer surface from the Dataverse Web API used for the flow definition itself).

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

workflow_id.description: Dataverse workflowid (GUID) of the flow whose runs to list.
workflow_id.title: Workflow Id

tools.name: get_flow_run
tools.description: Get details of one flow run by id, via the Power Platform REST API.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

tools.name: cancel_flow_run
tools.description: Cancel a currently running flow run.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

run_id.description: Flow run id to cancel, from list_flow_runs.
run_id.title: Run Id

tools.name: resubmit_flow_run
tools.description: Resubmit (re-run) a flow run with the same trigger inputs it originally received.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

run_id.description: Flow run id to resubmit (re-run with the same trigger inputs), from list_flow_runs.
run_id.title: Run Id

tools.name: bulk_set_flow_state
tools.description: Turn multiple cloud flows on/off in one call -- a value-add convenience this connector adds on top of Microsoft's API, which has no native bulk-state endpoint. Applies set_flow_state to each workflow_id in turn and reports success/failure per item.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

state.description: Target state for every listed flow: 'activated' (turn on) or 'suspended' (turn off).
state.title: State

tools.name: bulk_delete_flows
tools.description: Permanently delete multiple cloud flows in one call -- a value-add convenience this connector adds on top of Microsoft's API, which has no native bulk-delete endpoint. Deletes each workflow_id in turn and reports success/failure per item. This cannot be undone.

connection_id.description: Which connected environment to use. Omit if only one is connected.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

workflow_ids.description: Explicit Dataverse workflowids (GUIDs) to permanently delete; 1-100, never inferred.
workflow_ids.title: Workflow Ids

secrets.name: power_automate_connections
secrets.description: Your connected Power Platform environments -- stored as a JSON array, one entry per environment (Dev/Test/Prod etc), each with its own Azure AD App Registration (tenant_id, client_id, client_secret) and Dataverse environment_url/environment_id. Managed through connect_power_automate / disconnect_power_automate -- you should not need to edit this directly.
